utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You have half an hour to wind up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, frankly I think -- well, let's see how it will be. Because I have a -- I'll do my best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Ninkovic.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have, please, Exhibit P125?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, could you please look at page 3 of the copy of that Official Gazette? Could you please put it on the ELMO so that the others can follow this?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Pantelic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Article 5 of the Statute of the municipality speaks about certain celebrations and the traditions of the people of Posavina. I'm interested in the following: Could you please tell me, in relation to paragraph 2 of this paragraph -- of Article 5, and it says, in the municipality, other traditional celebrations are commemorated. In the period of 1993, in Samac, were the celebrations and other religious traditions of the other two peoples observed as well, that is to say the Muslim and the Croat peoples?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The authorities never interfered with that section of religious freedoms so the celebration of religious holidays was absolutely free and according to one's personal choice.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please look at paragraph 2 in the corner and could you please give a comment in this regard, if possible?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have nothing special to say here. I have already said that the authorities did not interfere with the religious convictions of their citizens, that is to say that citizens irrespective of their ethnic background could observe and celebrate their religious holidays and according to the Statute of the municipality, it was regulated what the official holidays were, of the municipality. It was only the day of the municipality. That is the only holiday that was observed at local level that was celebrated as the day of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The civilian authorities in the municipality of Samac, did they in any way prevent the observing of religious -- MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I object to this line of questioning. First of all, anything that arises out of the Statute speaks for itself. You can read it. But more importantly I didn't raise this issue in cross-examination. The issue that I raised in cross-examination when I referred to these gazettes was disenfranchisement of the non-Serb people. That was the issue. I didn't raise any issue regarding permission to carry on religious observance and so on. That wasn't raised at all in my cross-examination. It was only disenfranchisement and I did it in relation to the Statute and also you recall the local communes that those other two documents -- that was the only issue. Now we are going into something else. If this was important to Mr. Pantelic the proper time for it was in examination in chef, not now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Pantelic, the objection is observed. You must draw a distinction between examination-in-chief and re-examination. Re-examination, as the Prosecution pointed out, is only to clear matters raised in cross-examination. It's not an opportunity to continue examination-in-chief. Please do observe that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I am very well aware about that, Your Honour. But if you allow me, the religious rights of the citizens of Samac are also a part of general rights of citizens of Samac, so inevitably when I tried to find from this witness his personal knowledge of these facts are -- these facts are connected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The point is that was not raised in cross-examination. That's the point which the Prosecution is making and which the Trial Chamber agrees with.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Mr. Ninkovic, in Article 1, it says that the municipality of Samac is the municipality of the Serb people and other citizens living in it. Give me your comment with regard to this particular wording. Is there a certain parallel between certain constitutional solutions provided in Croatia and Slovenia? What about over there? Were the Serbs envisaged in these Statutes and other legislation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is well known thing that there are national states and civil states, and where there are civil states it is the state of all citizens, whereas where there is the national state it is the state of that nation and other citizens. This solution is a well known thing in the constitutions of many countries, and it is also directly related, for example, to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We are now into the relationship between the non-Croatian citizens in Croatia as well as the non-Slovenian citizens in Slovenia. I think this is well outside any relevance to this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, the objection is sustained. Please remain within the case, remain within the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour. I will do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, what about other citizens, non-Serbs, in 1992 and 1993? Could they exercise their civil rights in accordance with the law and constitution?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just going to repeat something in relation to your previous question. That is to say that Article 1 of this Statute is absolutely in accordance with the constitution of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and citizens could exercise their rights. That is to say irrespective of their ethnic and religious backgrounds, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My next question is related to the document that the Prosecutor showed you yesterday. That is P106. It has to do with abolishing Crisis Staffs in local communes in the territory of the municipality, if you remember that.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please, a few witnesses before you, explained in quite a bit of detail the reason for this decision. If you know, please tell me, during these first few months of 1992, April, May, do you know how many members of the Crisis Staff were there in different local communes? Can you -- I mean in villages, in local communes, can you tell me that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the motives for the Crisis Staff to pass this kind of decision was rationalisation of the number of these Crisis Staffs in the local communes, in view of the fact that there were five, six, seven, eight and some even ten persons, and many were military conscripts. So this was a considerable number of people altogether which practically did not have all that much to do. So that work could have been carried out by say one or two persons, so the objective was to reduce the number of persons involved. That is to say to carry out this rationalisation in terms of the allocation of different persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Ninkovic, as we heard you say yesterday, you were not a member, as you said, of the Crisis Staff. I wonder whether you could just very briefly say therefore how you know what the motives of the Crisis Staff were to pass, as you say, this kind of decision. How do you know the motives of the Crisis Staff were in your words rationalisation of the number of these small crisis staffs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I heard about that from people who, after that decision, were no longer members of crisis staffs of local communes, and who were given new war assignments. I assumed that they asked questions of Mr. Blagoje Simic and that is the information that they obtained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One set of the Prosecutor's questions had to do with the relationship between the executive council and the department of the Ministry of Defence and you spoke about that in considerable detail. Now, what I'm interested in is in the clarification of the following circumstances. First of all, we are talking about the frequency of meetings, and the relationship between the number of sessions of the assembly as one body on the one hand and the number of sessions of the executive council. Which one of the two met more often, in order to carry out their functions?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely these were sessions of the executive council, because this is the executive branch of the government which has to do with day to day issues, so they practically had meetings on a weekly basis, whereas the assembly meets whenever necessary. That is to say a month or two can go by between two different sessions of the assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you describe the period from April, 1992, until, say, the end of 1993, in Samac, there were different forms of local government, right? There was the Crisis Staff, the War Presidency, the municipal assembly. I'm interested in this entire period, and who met more often in Samac, was it the executive council, or these authorities that I mentioned, that is to say the Crisis Staff, the War Presidency, and the municipal assembly. Can you draw a parallel in that respect?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was not in a position to keep track of all of this, because I was not a member of the Crisis Staff and I don't know exactly how many meetings were held. Also, as for the executive council, I was invited every now and then only when the subject matter discussed had to do with what I had been dealing with. However, to the best of my knowledge, meetings of the executive council were held more frequently than those of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My next question has to do with the relationship between the department of the Defence Ministry that you headed and the executive council. You also spoke about that in detail when responding to the Prosecutor's questions. Now, what I'm interested in is the following: Could you describe for us in practice what this looked like, if regulations provide for some general matters? What was practice like in Samac? Did practice follow the regulations involved?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what you're getting at.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Or was practice something different? Please tell us what you know about this.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, under these circumstances, organs and institutions of the state usually resolve problems that crop up on the ground. They approach them in a practical way and often these regulations were not exactly accessible. That is to say problems were resolved on the ground so the executive council in that area had an operative role and true executive powers. I spoke about the relationship between the executive and the legislative branches and I said that it was the executive that had actual power. I said that to the Prosecutor when I was saying that the Prosecutor viewed the Crisis Staff as an organ which was practically in charge of all sorts of things. Quite simply that's not the way it was. The executive council also had its role, especially with regard to current day to day problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did this pertain to the work obligation as well, what you said just now?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because the executive council, by its very position, was in charge of resolving problems related to the economy of the municipality of Samac and it viewed the needs to engage labour. After all, it was the executive council that appointed general managers of companies, the executive council also adopted job descriptions for all companies, and all of this is directly related to work obligation as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My next question has to do with the following line of questioning of the Prosecutor. Namely the decision on the composition of members of the Crisis Staff. You gave your comment with regard to this Official Gazette, Official Gazette number 1, I believe, where the executive council composition was published. My question is the following: If the Crisis Staff is such an important and significant body, can you give us your comment on the basis of the knowledge that you have, why was a decision on the composition of the Crisis Staff never published in the Official Gazette? Can you help us with that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I testified here that as far as I know, there was never any definite composition or a list of that Crisis Staff, according to what I know, the Crisis Staff worked in sessions. People were called from different areas to participate in the work of the Crisis Staff when the work concerned those topics that they worked in. Perhaps there was an inner circle of the inner -- of the Crisis Staff where the people that we discussed here, but the number of people who worked in the Crisis Staff was greater, so these are probably the reasons why the composition was never published in the Official Gazette. I don't know what any other reason would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When the Prosecutor asked you about the position of Samac in Posavina, you mentioned a piece of information, if I'm not mistaken that the territory held by the Croat and Muslim forces west of the River Tinja, near Brcko, all the way to Brod, was of an area of 120 by 25 kilometres. Does that mean that this is a territory in square kilometres? I can't figure it out right now but could you please tell us roughly?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area of Posavina is about 3.000 square kilometres from the River Tinja along the Sava, along the length of 125 kilometres, 120, and the width is 25 kilometres. A part of the municipality of Samac which was not under the control of the Croat armed forces was about 170 square kilometres and that is about 6 per cent of the overall territory of Posavina, so everything else was under the control of the Croatian armed forces and the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You in response to questions from the Prosecution regarding the preamble of the document, when you were commenting on document P126?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit P126?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you thinking of the decision about the Crisis Staff which was signed by the President of the republic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one moment. That's page 3 of the gazette and you gave your comments about the position of the Prosecution, which have a theory that certain military operation was related to the takeover of power. We won't go back to that because you explained that clearly to the Prosecution. What I'm interested in generally is the question of this preamble and also, if you remember, the introductory remark signed by Mitar Mitrovic from the gazette published in 1994, and which talks about certain historical aspects. I'm interested, since you were in journalism what was the terminology of practically all the three sides during wartime in the 1992-93 period? How can you -- what can you? MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry to interrupt but I'm just confused about what's being put to the witness, P126 doesn't have the Mitar Mitrovic preamble. That's the previous exhibit, P125, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: 124, I believe, 124. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, 124, so it's not 126. And Exhibit 126 was produced to the witness. It's just not clear. It won't read clearly from the transcript in the future if we ever come back to look at it. So we should be clear, the Mitar Mitrovic preamble is in P124. What has been now placed before the witness, as I understand it, is P126 we just have to be clear about what's what.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact in order to avoid unnecessary number of exhibits in front of the witness, my idea is to explore this issue with regard to the terminology and the use of words and I tried to jog the memory of the witness with regard to the exhibit P124, the preamble which speaks about the history of the establishing of Serbian municipality and also with regard to the P126 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can go ahead and put whatever exhibit you are dealing with to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So as not to go into too many details, you recalled what I was talking about. So that's the declaration which was signed on Djordjija [phoen]. So this is what I would like you to tell us, since you did have contacts with the media, you were in journalism, how would you estimate in 1992 and 1993, the terminology used in the media of practically all the three warring sides? I'm specifically talking about Samac. We don't have to go broader.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: If it please Your Honours, a general dissertation on propaganda wasn't raised in cross-examination. And now is not the time for this witness to expound upon that. What was raised in cross-examination was specific passages from specific exhibits. Now if my learned friend wants to clarify anything relating to those passages or indeed giving him more latitude something else that arises in the preamble, fine, but not asking this witness to give his views on florid language that might have been used by warring sides in a war. That's not relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, the objection is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please look at page 4 of this Official Gazette? The signatory of this programme at the bottom is the signatory of the programme which starts on page 3 isn't that so? This is a programme -- I'm talking about the programme about the economic resolution of material resources.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This is page 3 of the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that page --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Turn -- turn back to the previous page and look at the heading, on the right. When you look at page 3, there is a problem with the copies. The whole number wasn't copied. So could you please turn to the next page? The Prosecutor asked you during cross-examination, he practically asked you the question of whether this was an act by -- a document by Blagoje Simic. If he was the signatory on the 24th of June, 1992 of this document, and many other documents, what is your comment? We already talked about this.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained that the presiding or the president of the assembly in the decision-making system has only one vote so the assembly adopts its documents by a majority out of the number of deputies who comprise that assembly. So this is a document of the municipal assembly which was adopted by a majority vote. I don't know what the vote was of the president of the assembly but as president of the assembly, it was his duty to sign each document which was adopted in the regular procedures of the assembly. So -- and that is the regular procedure in the assembly regardless of whether he voted for or against a particular document. So he was to sign the document according to regular procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next question is page 24, line 50 of yesterday's transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher you can take this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday on page 24 of the working version of the transcript, line 10, there is just a term which I would like to clarify which could maybe lead to some misunderstandings. The Prosecutor asked you about the forming of the special unit attached to the public security station in Samac and you explained that there never was such a special police unit of the MUP of Republika Srpska in Samac? MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, and Mr. Pantelic may have the advantage of me but -- because I don't have the transcript here and I assume he read it but I recall the witness saying he didn't know anything about such unit, not that there was no such unit rather that he didn't know anything about it. Didn't know of its existence that's a different thing from saying oh, no it doesn't exist. Unless I'm wrong that's my recollection of the evidence and it's quite an important distinction of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree with the Prosecution. That was the response of the witness, that he didn't know about it, but if he's changing his evidence that's okay with him, he can say what to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour, but my idea is to clarify the terminology between the Ministry of Interior of Republika Srpska and the other special unit of Ministry of Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina prior to the break-up of hostilities, so there is some imprecision in the transcript which I would like to clarify now. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, that's fine. I've got no problem with that but I don't want it being put to the witness or suggested to the witness that yesterday he said this special unit -- special purpose unit didn't exist. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Pantelic, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, do you have any personal knowledge about the presence of a special police unit in the period immediately prior to mid-April, 1992, in Samac? Do you have any personal knowledge about that? Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that police came from Sarajevo and they were deployed on the bridge over the River Sava but I don't know what kind of police forces they were, whether they were regular or special police forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. And after mid-April, 1992, in Samac, did you notice or did you hear or see any -- anything about any special police unit of MUP of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained yesterday that in the organisation of MUP, there was a special unit which was directly subordinated to the Minister of Internal Affairs. That unit was never located in the territory of the municipality of Samac and as far as I know they never came there. In Samac, as far as I know, there was no special unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Your time is over, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just a couple of seconds, reorganise the remaining of my topics? It won't be more than one or two questions. So I have to make a choice. Just -- I need just a couple of seconds, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding the arrest of Lugar, you talked about that with the Prosecutor. What is your personal knowledge about that operation? If you know. How was it conducted and how did the army manage to, in a way, remove -- how did the military bodies manage to remove Lugar and the other members of his unit from Samac? Because you were talking about the 1st Krajina Corps, the military formation which was in its area of responsibility there at that time. Do you have any personal knowledge about that operation? Did they come to Lugar and say, "Listen, you are under arrest and we are taking you away." Or was that conducted in a different way? What was done?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a change in the system of command and control because the 1st Krajina Corps subordinated the units from that area to its command. So that the command of the 2nd Posavina practically came under the command of the 1st Krajina Corps. I don't know any details about how he was arrested but I think that this was done by -- under instructions of the military Prosecutor by the military police of the 1st Krajina Corps from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So you don't know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He just said he doesn't know so he should not give us what he thinks. All right. We just want facts from him. The last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes my question was whether he has some personal knowledge about it. Could we have Exhibit D31/4 and D32/4, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are talking here about two letters which were introduced by my learned friend, Pisarevic, Mr. Zaric's defence attorney. They are letters, I don't know who wrote to whom first, but do you remember that you commented on them before the new year? You commented on the letter by the 2nd Posavina Brigade and your response or their response to your letter. Could you please look at those two documents that are in front of you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will first comment on my document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My question is as follows - and then you will have time to comment later. My question is as follows: Do you have any personal knowledge about certain occurrences and some activities by the military structures of the 2nd Posavina Brigade in relation to some political positions and activities in Samac in the course of 1992 and 1993? Just briefly tell us, please, without any detailed explanation what your personal knowledge is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Trying the best I can, if Your Honours please, I can't see how this topic arose in cross-examination yesterday or what evidence that this witness gave yesterday is being clarified by this now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, it was to be precise, Your Honour, it was a topic which was raised in cross-examination of one of the Defence teams so it was not directly related to the cross-examination of the Prosecution, but I have to clarify that because it was introduced through the other ways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Pantelic, you will be allowed to go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you heard my question. According to what you know, were there any indications or any activities by certain military structures in the territory of the municipality of Samac to participate in one way or another in the political life, yes or no? Could you please tell me?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please give me your comments on those two letters? Because one of the letters was authored by you. What is behind that correspondence? Could you please explain?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will explain the motive for my letter. At the time this document was written, the situation was very difficult in the war. The Croatian republic had several of its own brigades, there was the Zagreb Varazdin Brigade and some other brigades, I don't remember their names. The Army of Republika Srpska brought its 16th Brigade which was the best. At that time there was some serious battles on the front and there were deaths every day. To mobilise people into the war at that point was very difficult and people that I was a superior to had problems on the ground to mobilise people. If people who were being mobilised found out that there were people who were avoiding the draft or who were hiding their sons, it was very difficult, a very difficult period of work for the Ministry of Defence. The body at which -- where I was the chief, the son of Simo Zaric at that time was not under military obligation, and by his age, he was subject to military service, to military duty. According to the way I understand moral codes, it is not usual for the son of an officer who has a prominent position in the command of the brigade for morale and for patriotism for his son not to be fulfilling his military obligations. And this is the motive why I wrote this letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's the end of examination-in-chief. Thank you very much, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour just one last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, Mr. Pantelic we will go on. Thank you very much, Mr. Ninkovic, for giving evidence to the Tribunal. We are through with you. You may now go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before the next witness is called, I understand that the Prosecution have some matters they wanted to raise. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. The admission into evidence, if Your Honours please, of various documents. I've got some transcripts of the previous interviews. You recall the revamped version of the interviews which contained the B/C/S underneath each question and the B/C/S underneath each answer which will make it -- should the need arise I think it will make it easier to put to the defendants the remaining defendants. So could I introduce those into evidence? And then Mr. Re has some documentation that he wishes to see is tendered. Would Your Honours just bear with me for one moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So that's the end of your exhibits?

utterances.text: That have been pending. All right. If the -- after the numbering is done, that is off the bench, if there are any objections then the Defence can raise them. Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm speaking in my own name now. I don't know whether the other Defences will join me. Those that are formally taken into consideration. However, what I wish to say in relation to the further proceedings is the following: It is clear to me that according to Rule 85, paragraph A.3, that is Prosecution evidence rebutting Defence evidence, it is possible to introduce documents that were not disclosed to the other party previously, but I'm interested in the following: If during further proceedings, documents crop up that the Prosecution will want to introduce other documents that were not disclosed to the Defence, again I'm saying that I do not object to these particular documents, but if such additional evidence will be introduced later, can the Defence treat this as additional evidence and can we state our views with regard to them, whether we accept it or not? I think this would be in the interest of justice. If additional evidence is presented by the Prosecution that they did not disclose to the Defence previously, will it be possible for us to state our views? This has been presented to this Tribunal before, but I'm afraid that if through cross-examination, a document appears, and if it has to do, say, with my client or any other client, such a document had not been introduced or rather disclosed previously, will the Defence be able to state its views on its acceptability? This is my concrete question but I also have some other information for the Trial Chamber related to demography but perhaps I can deal with that later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It is obviously clear that if a document which has not been disclosed before, prior especially to the trial, and especially prior to the close of the Prosecution case, the Defence will have every right to raise issues with it and then the Trial Chamber can decide whether or not such a document should be admitted and be part of the evidence on record. That is the right of the Defence to do so. I just wanted to find out from the Prosecution whether indeed of the documents that have been presented today, there are any that had not been disclosed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No they have all been disclosed to the Defence, Your Honour and in addition to what Mr. Lukic just said, these are all public documents they are documents of which the Trial Chamber could take judicial notice except perhaps the ballot paper and they all arose as a result of questions I would have put to the two witnesses if I'd had more time and documents I would have put to professor Kecmanovic and Nikolic in the ordinary course of cross-examination. They are not in the nature of rebuttal evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Yes, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just explain. It is correct that this was disclosed to us but it was disclosed after the cross-examination so that is what I can understand as a possible problem. They were not disclosed previously but then I can appreciate that the Prosecutor deals with questions they want to raise during the cross-examination with a particular witness so really I do not object to that. But it may be disputable if things appear later that do not have to do with rule 94, and do we then have the right to state our views on such a document and how can we deal with the situation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I think I've already said that the Defence have a right to raise an issue with any document which appears out side after the time limits for such disclosure. Can we call the next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If I may add to this matter a few words? Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is it you want to say which Mr. Lukic hasn't said. I don't want to you repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I don't want to repeat. I just want to hear the position and the instruction of this honourable Trial Chamber with regard to this very important issue. My position and my opinion is that it's maybe better in order to protect the rights of the accused in this particular situation to take judicial notice of certain public documents, not to speculate what the other party or the Prosecution or Defence, whatever, might ask in cross-examination certain witness, because, Your Honour, --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pantelic, I'll cut you short because the rules of procedure are quite clear as to how the exhibits should be handled and they are quite clear as to what should be taken judicial notice of. Let's have the next witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, also, we have some other matters with regard to the witnesses, because our instruction.

utterances.text: Can we raise them after this witness?

utterances.text: We were instructed by the legal office to raise these issues in between two witnesses.

utterances.text: What, is the problem, then?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Between after the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. There is a witness waiting isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes of course but we got very precise instructions from the legal officer to raise certain procedural matters during the break between two witnesses. So that's why I'm raising this matters, Your Honour, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So it's a procedural matter, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, we have plenty of --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Registrar told me that you wished to be informed about my correspondence related to the demography expert so I wanted to inform you as to what I found out in the meantime. As I told the Trial Chamber before the recess, the Defence and the Prosecution have been informed by the OSCE that they gave their consent, as far back as the 6th of December, to look at the documentation that they provided to the Prosecution. So that is not being challenged in any way. But finally, on January 6th, we got this other answer which I had expected all the time, and which was controversial and that is the answer of the federal institution for statistics of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This is a short letter. I'll read it to you and I've also given it so that it could be translated in writing but it is a -- I have the version in B/C/S now, so I'm going to read it out so that you can hear it. The letter is dated the 6th of January, 2003. It says, "Reference, the census of Bosnia-Herzegovina of 1981 for the municipalities of Bosanski Samac and Odzak." It is addressed to my office. "Dear sir, the federal institution for statistics -- the federal institution for statistics, as an administrative organisation of the government of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina provided the Office of the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for crimes committed in the territory of the former Yugoslavia, data from the census of Bosnia-Herzegovina of 1991 on the basis of approval given by the government of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, namely the federal institution for statistics according to the law on the organisation and implementation of the census of 1991 does not have the authority to disclose the mentioned data to third parties. In view of the extraordinary circumstances involved in Bosnia-Herzegovina for having the data mentioned disclosed, we need to have approval by the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Could you please address the Trial Chamber that would observe the required procedure, address a request to the government of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina with a view to obtaining approval to look at the required documents? Respectfully yours, director, Dervis Djurdjevic, professor," and then there is a stamp of that institution and a signature. That is the content of the letter that I obtained on the 6th of January in my office. I just wish to mention to you what the technical aspect of what we need requires so that the Trial Chamber would rule on that. Several times during the recess I talked to Mrs. Svetlana Radovanovic, our court expert, who has been working on this matter for a long time now and she is supposed to look at these documents as Mrs. Ewa Tabeau did, and to give her opinion on the basis of the review of these data. According to Svetlana Radovanovic's opinion and according to the expertise provided by Mrs. Tabeau, she said that she needed two additional computer experts because obviously the data were processed by computer. She said that she would need three working days to carry out this analysis for the municipalities of Samac and Odzak. If she works with one computer expert, then perhaps it would require an additional day. What I suggested last time to the Trial Chamber was that irrespective of any decision you may pass, and irrespective of the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, namely that our expert takes an oath before this Trial Chamber involving everything that Rule 77 entails, and that therefore our expert could look at the required documents. So could our expert do the same that Mrs. Ewa Tabeau did and I think that in this way we could get information more quickly. Also after insight as to this documentation we would have an expert opinion within ten days so within about 15 days the opposing party would get this expertise. Without getting this approval, we will have great difficulty in developing our own expert opinion with regard to this important matter on which the Prosecution already stated its views through its expert witness. So could we please be instructed as to whether the Defence should address the government of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Will it be the Trial Chamber or is there any other course of action that should be taken? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we go into private session so we complete this matter?

utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the witness?

utterances.text: Your Honour, I do apologise. I have also to inform the Trial Chamber about certain witness list according to the instruction of the legal officer.

utterances.text: Yes, can you go ahead?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I would like to -- because they didn't finish.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence has received a motion from the --

utterances.text: So you're just asking for extension of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It is granted, as the Court has suggested, on Monday. Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, first of all with regard to the lineup of Defence witnesses, today, we shall have next witness who is waiting his name is Dusan Tanasic. utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, you do that in writing you simply put your list of witnesses in the order you have decided and you file that. That's all you have to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: During yesterday's conversation with our learned friends, I raised the issue of our handwriting expert, professor Aleksic. utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No problem. And just for the -- sorry.

utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and just for the record, in reorganisation of the list of the witnesses for 92 bis, Rule 71 and viva voce, it arose the fact that one witness was not previously on the list, and according to the instructions of the legal officer of this Trial Chamber, just for the record I would like to mention the name. utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just for the record.

utterances.text: Yes is there any objection from the Prosecution? Because this witness was not on the previous, the first filed list of witnesses of the Defence. MR. DI FAZIO: Just as I stand here, I don't know anything about this particular witness.

utterances.text: Just to help just for the record and also it might be help of assistance to our learned friends, in fact, Mrs. Pelka Andric will replace Nezirovic, Dusanka. utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.text: Very well, since we have only a few minutes we will take our break earlier and start at 11.25 hours with the next witness.

utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can hear you very well.

utterances.text: Very well. I have understood what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tanasic, could you please introduce yourself by your full name and surname?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I am Dusan Tanasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You were born on the 8th of September, 1958, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You were born in the territory of the municipality of Samac in Gornji Zabar?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I have to correct you. Gornji Zabar is now Pelagicevo and the municipality is Gradacac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. You're a Serb by ethnicity, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What about your parents? Are they also from the same area where you were born?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes. My parents and my ancestors.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So your roots go back a few centuries in that particular area, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes. We've been living there for generations now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You completed elementary school in Pelagicevo, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, in Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What about secondary school? You completed it in Bijeljina, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I completed two secondary schools, the first one in Gradacac, a general high school, and the second one in Bijeljina, a vocational school for agriculture and technical studies.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You also completed a higher school of management in Prijedor, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You did your military service in the JNA in 1982 in Slovenia, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, in Slovenia, in Crnomelj.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That was a unit for atomic, chemical, and biological defence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have a military rank?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Well, a low one, sergeant.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Tanasic, are you knowledgeable, as far as radio communication is concerned? When did you first express such interests? What kind of diplomas do you have? Do you have anything specific to tell us in this respect, with regard to this, that you have been dealing with?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: As far back as the beginning of elementary school, secondary school, I have been involved in electronics. I am a ham radio operator. And as of recent, I have been dealing with computers as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So for almost 20 years now you've had experience in the area, right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, approximately that much, perhaps even a bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I assume that as a ham radio operator, and as a person who is well-versed in this area, you have a registered radio station of your own and that is how you communicate with your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: No. I haven't got that actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is there a club or something else, where you engage in this hobby of yours, if I can put it that way?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: As the former Yugoslavia fell apart, this sort of dwindled away.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: However, until 1992, I assume that you functioned within a club?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Until the beginning of the war, 1992, you worked as an employee in the Napredak company; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's in Pelagicevo. Where is the seat of that company?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: The seat of that company is in Gradacac. There is only one branch in Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. So that was the situation until 1992?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, professionally speaking, what have you been doing professionally since April 1992? You can tell us about the segments involved. You don't have to go into each and every company but for example where did you work? I assume that during the war, in 1992, you were mobilised. And how much time did you spend in the military unit?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: From April, 1992, until the end of April, 1993, I worked as head of communications in a military unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just tell me which military unit this was. Was it a detachment? Was it a company? What was its name?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Its official name was the 3rd Detachment of the 17th Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: However, when the Army of Republika Srpska was established in May, 1992, how was this unit named or perhaps was it a different unit then?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: This unit was called the 2nd Posavina Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you say until August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I said April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. I misheard you. After April, 1993, what duties did you have professionally speaking?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: After April, 1993, I worked as head of communications at the police station, at the public security station in Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Until when?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Until the present day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Who was Chief of Police, who was chief of that police station in Pelagicevo during the period of your employment, say from April 1993 until the end of 1993?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: The head of the station was Radul Radulovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: From the point of view of hierarchy, how were you linked up? Did you have within the Ministry of the Interior some kind of setup? I mean what was your superior command so to speak? Who was above the public security station in Pelagicevo?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Above the station in Pelagicevo was the centre of public security in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know about the following? The centre of public security in Doboj, can you tell me what Doboj covered actually? Just give me a few examples. What was the region that was covered by the public security centre in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: The Doboj centre covered Pelagicevo, Samac, Modrica, Teslic, Petrovo, Derventa, and Vukosavlje.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to know who headed the centre of public security in Doboj from April, 1993, onwards, when you came, or rather until the end of 1993? Do you happen to know? It's not that relevant but I'm just asking you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was Andrija Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me is there any organisational form that is above the Doboj public security centre? Who were they accountable to? So what is the hierarchy involved?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Above the public security centre was the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us go back to the period from April, 1992, until April, 1993. What was your position in the military unit called the 2nd Posavina Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I was head of communications. That is chief of group for communications in the 3rd Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And who was commander of that detachment?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: The commander was Mirko Dragic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, the 2nd Posavina Brigade, with its detachments, if you know and I'm particularly interested in the 3rd Detachment, where were they from originally, the members of the 3rd Detachment? Where were they born? And also members of the 2nd Posavina Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: The members of the 3rd Detachment were from Pelagicevo, Samarevac, Blazevac, Porebrice.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So the soldiers were born in the territory of the villages that you mentioned, is that true?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And where was Mirko Dragic, the commander, from?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: From Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please tell me a little bit about your political engagement? When did you become a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you have any post in the party?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was the chairman of the municipal board for Gradacac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, Gradacac is to the south of Samac and Pelagicevo. Maybe some 20 kilometres away, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you go to Gradacac often at the time when you became the chairman of that municipal board? In what year was that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: In 1990, in August.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you go to Gradacac often in the period of 1990 and 1991? Could you please describe to us what your work was as the chairman of the municipal board?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I went to Gradacac very often. And besides regular party duties, there was also a lot of interparty activity. Since at that time, together with the Croat and Muslim parties, we participated in the administration in power, after the first multi-party elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did SDS participate in Gradacac in power at the local level after the multi-party elections in 1990 in Bosnia-Herzegovina? Did SDS participate in the local authorities in Gradacac?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes. The SDS had the chairman of the executive board, the chief of the administration for budget, the police commander, and some other lesser posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How would you describe briefly, based on your personal knowledge, the atmosphere in Gradacac and Pelagicevo in that region in the period since the multi-party elections in 1990, up to the end of 1991?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: The entire time, the Muslim and Croat parties immediately, and this was evident, reached some kind of agreement and immediately initiated joint activities relating to the break away of Bosnia from the then Yugoslavia, and since they had a larger number of deputies, they would over -- use the majority vote.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: At that time, was there a principle of equality or the principle of the protection of the equality of peoples, even at the local level?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: No. That principle did not exist. Voting was simply conducted and the side that had more votes would have its way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was there the obligation at the local level to respect the interests of all three peoples?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, but formally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, after --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, just for clarification, I wonder whether Mr. Tanasic could explain what his answer means, where, on line 9 of page 44, in response to your question concerning the obligation at the local level to respect the interests of all three peoples, his answer is, "Yes, but formally." I'm not too certain what that means. Maybe you could clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You heard Her Honour, Judge Williams, Mr. Tanasic, could you please explain that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. According to the constitution that was then in force, we all had exactly the same rights. However, decisions at the local level were adopted by simple outvoting. So there was no possibility for us to protect our interests, which were threatened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, also I wonder whether Mr. Tanasic you could maybe tell us, did each person at these various meetings have one vote? There was one vote for each member? Was that so? Or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. One deputy, one vote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And also, the persons who were the deputies had been freely elected by the local population? Was that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: So therefore, was the majority, in terms of the ones who you say voted and together outvoted one other group, they had been freely elected and then were therefore exercising their one vote as they saw fit? Would that have been the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understood you properly, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you familiar with the principle of the equality of the constitutive peoples in Bosnia-Herzegovina? And I'm speaking about the period from 1990 until 1992.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, in general terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, Mr. Tanasic, when, if you know, when the deputies of the Serb parties in the fall of 1992 [as translated] left the republican parliament? How did that event reflect at the local level on the political atmosphere? If you know, of course. And there is a correction, just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: There is one correction to the transcript. In my question on line 45, line 18, instead of fall of 1992, should be fall of 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we are talking about the fall of 1991, when the Serb deputies left the republican parliament. How did this reflect on the local political level? Could you please tell us your personal knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: After the republican deputies left the parliament of Bosnia and Herzegovina, an assembly of the Serbian people of Bosnia and Herzegovina was established, and that assembly issued an instruction that at the local level, municipalities of the Serbian people should be established.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please tell me if you have any personal knowledge about the plebiscite of the Serbian people in November, 1991, and if you are familiar with that, was this conducted in the area where you are from?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes. The plebiscite was conducted in our territory, and in -- and 99 per cent or more of the population voted in favour of remaining in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. You said that you were in the Napredak company until the break -- the war broke out, but could you also please tell me, in the period at the end of 1991 and up until April, 1992, were you also a military -- subject to military service? Were you in the military reserves?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes. From December, 1991, I was mobilised as a member of the reserves into the 17th Tactical Group at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: The commander was Stevan Nikolic. I think he was a Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was the 17th Tactical Group a military formation within the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was. It was a part of the then Tuzla Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What can you tell us about the response to the call-ups in that period? And I'm talking about the different ethnic groups. Could you please tell us what you saw, what you know personally about that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: The military units called up all those subject to military service, and that included all the peoples. However, almost exclusively Serbs responded to the call-ups.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were there any cases that Muslims and Croats responded to the call-ups and if they did respond, to which military formations were they called into?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: There were a few cases, so there was an officer in the command who was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The 17th Tactical Group had several detachments. Do you know how many?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: It had four detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And could you please tell me where you were in the detachment, in the period from the end of 1991 until April, 1992? And could you please describe what you found out then when you were working at your post? What did you know about the situation at the time in the Samac region?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I was in charge of the radio stations, which monitored the radio communications in the area of the Serb municipalities, in the Posavina municipalities, and in that period, there was a lot of radio communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's on page 47, line 22 I didn't hear the witness mention Serb municipalities and things like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have that corrected? Yes, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour I'm objecting to the evidence my learned friend Mr. Pantelic is leading in relation to radio communications and monitoring of radio communications. The Defence motion in respect of the revised witness list filed on the 12th of November, 2002 in response to the Trial Chamber's order to give notice to the Prosecution of the facts to be adduced gives -- this is on page 7, gives absolutely no notice of anything in relation to this witness's now appears very important role in monitoring radio communications, nor his role in the military. According to the summary provided, Mr. Tanasic was a vice-president of the Serb municipal assembly of Samac and Pelagicevo and acting president for several weeks in 1992. He will testify the following facts. Nothing to do with the military situation and radio communications. We have had no notice of this, of these important facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, it's not testimony with regard to the isolated events. It's rather his experience that he was a member of military unit and then just a simple picture of that. I'm not going to explore that in details. Just general -- general and personal knowledge of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let me take this opportunity also, because I was observing that when you call a witness, you are calling a witness to testify on the allegations against the accused, not give his own personal history, right? And then in this -- with what Mr. Re raised indeed on your summary there is nothing to do with monitoring radio communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: As I said, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you limit to what you subscribed to in the summaries and you limit the evidence of the witness to the defence on the allegations against the accused because you're taking your time discussing other things and this witness is timed for one hour. And that is your list.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You go ahead and stick to the matters in the summaries and also to the defence, not the history and the activities of the witness, they should be related to the defence of the accused. So you have -- you timed this witness for one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but allow me just to ask for the -- your instructions, of course. Previously, the Defence for Blagoje Simic, Mr. Blagoje Simic, got certain number of hours. Certain number of witnesses I already cut below the designated hours so I kindly ask not to stick so formally to this estimation of time for particular witness, hour and a half maybe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, because you see, Mr. Pantelic, the hours that were given by the Defence counsels will have to be complied with because the other witnesses have their hours varied so we can't go once witness comes on the scene, then the hours are varied. That won't do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's one hour for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe the totality of hours we have to follow. I mean in general, after the presentation of the case, we shall be, I think, around or less, the estimated hours. That was my approach.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That has already been calculated by the Trial Chamber. And each witness is timed and those are the hours given.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And also, if you allow me, forcible takeover is one of the forms of the persecution and then I'm going directly to the issue of the Defence of my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can proceed but this witness was timed for one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And therefore, I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Just proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I don't believe, Your Honour, that I will be able to finish this witness in one hour. Believe me. I mean I have to discuss some official gazettes with him and please be -- let's see how it will be and then let's consider that maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, the point is you are the one who indicated one hour for this witness. The other witnesses, and he has jumped the list. You have revised the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So the other witnesses are five hours, the other witnesses are three hours, who were supposed to be called before him, so it's not like we are cutting down on your time, no. You indicated these hours yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you can understand my position, Your Honour. In totality I will be more or less around the totality of hours or maybe half an hour more or less, you will see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You will see what the lines are and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Mr. Tanasic, in your engagement in this military unit, what did you learn through monitoring these conversations as a radio operator? Can you just tell us briefly?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: We discovered the deployment of the Croatian forces in the villages surrounding Samac and that they had been preparing themselves to capture the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In mid-April, to be more precise, on the night between the 16th and 17th of April, 1992, where were you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I was at the command post at this very same radio station and I monitored the developments.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So what was the -- what were the developments?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Again I object to this, Your Honour. It's exactly the same issue I raised a few moments ago. The Prosecution has no notice of the monitoring of these alleged radio interceptions, which apparently now are forming an important part of the Defence case. The Defence has had a long time to structure its summaries and what it was going to lead evidence of and this is the first time we've heard of this while we are in court today. This was the matter which I understand Your Honour ruled upon a few moments ago. There was to be no evidence on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic please stick to your summaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, Mr. Tanasic, you were -- you were elected as an official of the Serbian Municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, when did that take place?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: On the 29th of February, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, in that period, so from early 1992 until, let's say, mid-April of 1992, where did you spend most of your time? What was -- what were your basic duties? From January, 1992 until April, 1992, you worked in a company but you also told me that you were mobilised for the 17th Tactical Group, and you were an official of the Serbian Municipality of Pelagicevo in the making. So tell me, which duty did you devote most of your time to in that period?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I did not work in the company. Most of my time I spent in the military unit, and my free time I was -- during my free time I was engaged in party activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: At that time, was the municipality of Pelagicevo established? I'm talking about February 1992 onwards.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: The municipality of Pelagicevo was established as late as the 12th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And who was the President of the municipal assembly of Pelagicevo municipality?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: The President was Milan Babic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That is -- that was not the Milan Babic from Krajina?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: No. That was Milan Babic from Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, at this founding session that took place on the 29th of February, if I'm correct, in 1992, who was present, what was discussed, what decisions were taken? Can you tell us anything about that, if you can recall, where the session was held, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: The session took place in the memorial centre called Mitar Trifunovic, Uco, and present there were deputies from -- deputies from the Serbian people of the municipality of Samac, Gradacac, and Orasje.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, who was elected president of this newly established Serbian Municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo municipality in the making?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Dr. Ilija -- I can't remember just now his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You mean Dr. Ilija Risic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were you also elected at that time to some position?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I was elected vice-president.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was Dr. Blagoje Simic also elected at the time to discharge certain duties?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Before that, let me ask you, what this session, generally known to the public, was that an open session or was that held in secrecy?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: No. It was completely public.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, what was the reaction of the population, of the local population, regarding this session? If you have any personal knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the reaction was positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: At this session of the 29th of February -- 28th of February, 1992, can you remember which decisions were taken and what kind of documents were adopted?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly which decisions were taken but I do know that none of that was implemented. It was more or less in the form of a declaration, in declaratory form.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, was there another session held of this newly established Serbian municipal assembly of Samac and Pelagicevo in the making?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Precisely because the elected assembly did not do anything, the following session was held on the 28th of March in Obudovac, but similarly, this also failed. This assembly didn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us something about whether at this second session, held on the 28th of March, 1992, was the executive council of the Serbian assembly elected?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes. The executive council was elected, but just so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: At this session, was Dr. Ilija Risic still the President?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: No. At this second -- at this session, Dr. Ilija Ristic resigned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did he offer any rationale for his resignation and can you remember what he said?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that his reasons were due to his health.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: At the time, you were the vice-president of the municipality. Did you take over chairing of the session? And I'm referring to the one held on the 28th of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes. Since Ilija -- Dr. Ilija Ristic resigned, I took over the chair of the session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, we are going to discuss an Official Gazette?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: P124, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the Official Gazette of the Samac municipality number 1, and in it, various decisions were published, the rules of procedure of the municipality, the decision on its founding, et cetera, so I would kindly ask you if we can comment on some of these decisions. On page 1, or in fact, as it is the page 4 of the paper that you have, there is a decision on the founding. Do you remember that on the session of the 29th of February, was this decision adopted to establish the municipality of the Serbian people of Samac and Pelagicevo in the making?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, this kind of decision was not adopted at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you please explain that to me? How come, then, that this decision exists as the one taken in the February? You were after all the vice-president of the assembly. How can you explain that? Why was it published here?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: This Official Gazette was published in the year 1994. And it contains many things that were in fact not adopted at the time. I presume that that was included or inserted at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you please go to page 10 of your exhibit? Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You can see number 8, that's decision number 8, in the middle of the left column, and refers to the election of the President of the municipal assembly. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And it says here that you were elected vice-president of the municipality as of 28th of March, 1992. What's your comment on this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: This is completely wrong, because I was elected on the 29th of February at the first session, and I was elected vice-president.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at this document. Look at page 1, please. Could you leaf through it? Could you see what was adopted? And please give me your comments so that we wouldn't move from one item to the other. What was discussed at the sessions of the 29th of February and the 28th of March, since you were a direct participant and you held the position that you held, so could you please give us a comment?
