What was adopted, what was discussed, and in your opinion, what is it that does not correspond to the actual state of affairs, in terms of what was actually going on?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: The first thing that I cannot but see is the following. There are some decisions here on the establishment of crisis staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, where did you find that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: On page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This page 1 is the preamble that was done in 1994 but I'm interested in the subsequent decisions.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Not at a single one of these sessions were any Crisis Staffs established.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Specifically, please look at page number 8, and you can see number 5, this is decision number 5. It doesn't have a special name. It just says it's a decision. In the capacity of vice-president, you are mentioned here. This is some kind of Crisis Staff that is mentioned here but I'm just asking you about the session of the 28th of March, 1992. That is where you were vice-president of the assembly of the municipality. Was this kind of decision discussed? Was this kind of decision adopted, a decision with this kind of content?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: There was absolutely no discussion about this, or was a decision of this kind adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Nevertheless, can you remember? It's been about ten years now. Can you remember what was discussed and what was adopted on the 28th of March, 1992, at the session of the municipal assembly? What was discussed?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Elections were carried out. The executive council was elected. And most of the time was taken up by the allocation of positions among these territories of ours, the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, this executive board, did it function in the period starting from the 28th of March, 1992, onwards?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: No. Just like before that, this executive council did not function.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Tanasic, when was the municipality of Pelagicevo formed? I think you said it was in May of 1992. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was the 12th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And until when did it function? What happened there in relation to the work of that assembly?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Already at the beginning of June, we got a ban in writing related to the work of the assembly, by the then commander of the 2nd Posavina Brigade, Dragan Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was his nickname?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Crni.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How come? How did you interpret that? How could a person who held a military position ban the functioning of a municipality? What did you do about it? Who did you contact in this respect?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I and the president of the executive council, Mirko Davidovic, went to the command of the corps to complain. However, the commander of the corps, Colonel Dencic stood behind the decision taken by his subordinate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know who appointed Crni commander of the 2nd Posavina Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes. The then commander of the corps, Colonel Dencic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, we have agreed to give you another half hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So 12.00 or 13.00 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much Your Honours. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, what was done then at the level of the municipality of Pelagicevo by the officials that you mentioned after this meeting with Dencic? Did the municipality continue to operate or did something else happen?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: No. This municipality ceased to operate. And the then officials were persecuted in a special way by these special units.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you mention who the -- when you mention these special units, who are you referring to? Who were these people? Can you give us some names?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I mean that unit, which was headed by Lugar and these volunteers from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, were there any subsequent attempts made for the civilian authorities from Pelagicevo to address superior commands, attempting to resolve the situation, as it was?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I did not directly participate in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If you know, could you tell us who it was who made these attempts? After all, you were president of the local committee, the municipal committee of the SDS rather, so I imagine you knew who it was who tried to resolve the problem.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: This elected president of ours, Milan Babic, took action in that direction, and in fact this action did yield some results.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Tanasic, when the war conflict broke out in mid-April, 1992, in the Samac municipality, what do you know about the work of the municipal Crisis Staff? Do you have any personal knowledge in this respect?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Very little. My knowledge is insignificant.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was a Crisis Staff established in Pelagicevo as well, one that covered that territory?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: No, in Pelagicevo, one was not established.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What can you tell us about how the SDS party practically ceased to operate or rather how it was banned in this war situation? When did this happen and what is your personal knowledge in this regard?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: As soon as the conflict broke out, I think it was the beginning of March, all the political parties were banned by the republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was a meeting held in respect of that, a meeting of party structures in the region, a meeting regarding this decision? And if so, what was discussed at the meeting? What happened?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: No. No meeting was held.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you remember any contacts or meetings in the building of the municipality of Bosanski Samac sometime in March, April, 1992, in the presence of all the other heads of party from the region? Were you there? And what happened?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that meeting, which was held in the municipality building in Samac. It was attended by the representatives of municipalities -- the municipalities of Samac and Gradacac, Orasje and Odzak, and it was held within the efforts made to find a peaceful solution within the Cutilheiro plan. It had to do with some kind of cantonisation of the area of Posavina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, I assume that you attended that meeting as one of the helmsmen of the SDS from that territory; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes. The President of the municipality of Gradacac, Sefko Mesanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What is his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What party was he from?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: The Party of Democratic Action.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Who else was there from that territory?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: The President of the Croat Democratic Union and the president -- the representatives of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And what was the atmosphere like at that meeting? Or actually can I ask you before that, were there any representatives of the military?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, a representative of the military was there, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How many members of the military were there in total at the meeting in the corridors, in front of the building? Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, at the meeting, there was one officer, and I assume that he came in a military jeep and that makes a total of four to five persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were they armed and did they threaten the participants of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: No. They were in attendance as observers more or less, without any active participation in the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How could you describe the atmosphere at the meeting itself?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: In my opinion, the atmosphere was good. In response to one of the proposals to divide up different spheres of interest, whereby it was proposed that somehow the Serbs obtained the town of Samac, the Muslims obtained Gradacac, and the Croats Orasje and Odzak, my impression was that the representatives of the Muslims were in favour of adopting that proposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you have any knowledge regarding the following? Was another municipality of Bosanski Samac established in the territory of the pre-war municipality of Bosanski Samac? And if you know about this, what is the name of this municipality?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact name but the Croats did establish some municipality of their own, some municipality of Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, after this meeting ended, what kind of comments did the participants in the meeting make? Could you describe the atmosphere to us a bit, specifically were there any tensions, squabbles? Was there any anger? Were people shouting? Can you describe this to us?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: No. At the meeting, the representatives of the Croats vehemently opposed that proposal, whereas after the meeting, there were normal discussions, and we all went out for a drink together.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was Dr. Blagoje Simic present?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What kind of positions did he take? What did he have to say in the discussion?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: He was in a normal mood.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did he present any ultimatum?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did he threaten anybody?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did he blackmail anybody in any way? Did he blackmail the present representatives?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. This is just.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to the leading, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, you should rephrase your questions. Avoid a leading question, which is suggestive of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please tell me, in the period 1991 or to be precise in the period from the summer of 1990 until April, 1992, did you meet Dr. Blagoje Simic? Did you see him?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes. We did. We met. And we saw each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On what basis?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Informally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were these official contacts also?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the period?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It was from the summer of 1990, until April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: From 1990 until 1992, we had a lot of meetings, official meetings, as presidents of political organisations, and together we participated in the creation of a regional party organisation for Posavina, which included several municipalities, Samac, Gradacac, and Orasje.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you personally have any knowledge about an instruction or a document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in the transcript, page 63, line 6 -- let me see now. Your first question concerned the period from 1991 to 1992, and then you said -- you extended it on line 15 back to 1990, or which period do you intend to ask about? From 1990 or from 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That was my mistake in phrasing the question. Actually, we are covering period from the mid-of 1990 until the April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in that period, you had contacts. Could you please tell me, do you have any personal knowledge? And now I'm talking about the period from December, 1991, until April, 1992, about an instruction or direction from the higher SDS authorities about -- to the Crisis Staffs, about some kind of Variant A or Variant B? Do you know anything about any such instruction?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I did not receive that, and I didn't hear anything about -- anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit P3, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meantime, could you please tell me, in the contacts with Dr. Blagoje Simic, did he voice any discriminatory intentions towards non-Serb citizens generally in the municipality of Samac, in conversations with you, official and private ones?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before the witness answers, again it's a leading question. He's entitled to ask about Dr. Simic but not to put the words in his mouth like that. There is only one answer that is going to come from this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, can you rephrase your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Tanasic, I'm asking you what is your personal knowledge in contacts with Dr. Blagoje Simic, about his position or relationship towards other ethnic communities.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I personally, and also Dr. Blagoje Simic, were primarily of a pro-Yugoslav stance, which meant total equality of all the peoples and naturally no discrimination, either in our position or anything else. The majority -- most of our activities in the Serbian Democratic Party were oriented towards the preservation of that common state, and one of our main activities was to organise the plebiscite in favour of remaining within Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the document in front of you, look through it, look at the heading, the title -- the date and the signature? Did you ever see this document before?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: No. I've never seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Take this exhibit, I've finished with it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tanasic, could you please tell me, was there any -- if you know, of course -- any cooperation and coordination, were there any plans, public or secret ones, between the SDS and the JNA in that region, in the period of 1991 and 1992? Do you have any knowledge about that, in view of the fact that you were an official of the SDS? Was there any secret activity or any secret plans in this regard?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: No. I am not aware of anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge about whether Dr. Blagoje Simic actively participated in the sending of some young men and volunteers from the municipality of Samac for military training outside of the Samac area?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: No. Dr. Blagoje Simic held the position even which was contrary to the position of the army at that time. He was not in favour of that JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were there any cases that people were sent for training outside of the territory of the Samac municipality, and if so, did you know who organised it and so on, and if you don't know, just say so.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Afterwards, when that one group arrived, then we found out that this had taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what you found out? Who was the main person who organised the sending of these people away for training?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: As far as what I heard, the person in charge was Stevan Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How would you describe the relations between the civilian structures, the political structures, and the military bodies in the period of April, 1992, until the end of 1993? What I'm interested in, if you know, is for you to tell us who issued orders to whom, and how did all of this function, if you know, could you please give us a description?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: The army was above the civilian authorities and there was no possibility of the civilian authorities issuing orders to the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, after the corridor was broken through in the summer of 1992, which military formation had its area of responsibility in the territory of the Samac, Odzak, and Pelagicevo municipalities? So this was after the corridor was broken through.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was the Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, if you know, when the municipal assembly of Samac started to function? When did the sessions begin? When did the committees begin to work? And so on?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So you don't know when this began, in what year?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I don't know but I think it was in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, you were the President of this municipal committee?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Once the witness says he doesn't know, he should not be allowed to start speculating. Either he knows what happened or he doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I absolutely follow this principle but his answer was I'm not sure so that was the motive for me to clarify that because if he said yes or no, that would be -- I don't know. But I'm not sure. My guess was maybe he's not sure about the year or dates. That's why I proceeded with this line of questioning. But this fact is not in dispute so I think that it's not contentious. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I wanted to ask you is that you at that time were the President of the municipal board of the SDS. How long were you in that post, until when?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Until the work of the party was banned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And after that, were you elected into any SDS bodies after May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: When the party work was reactivated, I was again the President of the municipal board.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I think this was in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And until when were you president of the municipal board?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Until 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me briefly how would you describe, based on your personal knowledge, Dr. Blagoje Simic as a person, based on your contacts with him?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: A moderate politician, a calm person, and probably because of his profession, a humanist.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tanasic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour it's time for our break, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, and that's the end of examination-in-chief. Cross-examination this afternoon will start. It will be one hour and then re-examination. We will rise until 1430 hours. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.01 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It's the Prosecution's cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Tanasic, my name is David Re from the Prosecution. I'm going to ask you some questions about the evidence you gave a little earlier. Just before the lunch break, you described -- you were asked to describe Dr. Blagoje Simic's character or his personality and you described him as a moderate politician, a calm person, and probably because of his profession, a humanist. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And also, you described him as a person who wasn't prone to discrimination against other ethnicities. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If the Crisis Staff or War Presidency, of which Dr. Simic had been a part, had issued orders or participated in the detention of Croats and Muslims, based solely upon their ethnicity, the isolation of Croat people, based solely upon their ethnicity, the inhumane treatment of Muslims and Croats in detention, solely upon their ethnicity, deported Croats and Muslims from their homes, based solely upon their ethnicity, ordered or participated in the forced labour at the front line of Muslims and Croats, solely upon their ethnicity, and ordering or participating in the taking of their homes and their property from them, if Dr. Simic and the Crisis Staff of which he was part had ordered or participated in any of those things, would you have to agree that they were discriminatory things and you would have to alter your opinion of him, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. It's a pure speculation. I mean he's calling for speculation. Maybe he can be more specific what is the personal knowledge of this witness with regard to certain events or certain decisions or orders or behaviour and then we could have a proper examination. Otherwise, he's calling for, if the War Presidency or Crisis Staff et cetera, et cetera. I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, your objection is misconceived. Those are the allegations of the Prosecution against Dr. Blagoje Simic so it's proper to put them to the witness in cross-examination. Mr. Re, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you understand my question, Mr. Tanasic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: No. There were too many words. I actually don't know what you asked me. It was a much too long question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your evidence was that Dr. Simic was a humanist, a person who doesn't engage in discriminatory behaviour. That's your opinion of him, correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That is based upon what you say you know about him, correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, if he had participated in discriminatory behaviour during 1993 and -- sorry, 1992 and 1993, such as ordering the detention of Muslims and Croats only because they were Muslims and Croats, you would agree that that would be discriminatory, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: If he did participate, but I don't know what he was doing after the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If he had done that, you would have to alter your opinion of him as a nondiscriminatory humanist, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In the period leading up to April the 17th, 1992, that is the period, the months just before then, ethnic tensions were running fairly high in Bosnia and in the municipality of Bosanski Samac, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the meeting which was -- I'm sorry, the division of Bosnia Herzegovina on ethnic lines was a fairly emotional issue in early 1992, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. What do you mean, ethnic or national?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: National and along the lines of Serb, Croat, or Muslim, the division of Bosnia-Herzegovina into cantons or areas based upon ethnicity was an emotional issue and one that was discussed, correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Before the war broke out, the discussions had been within the efforts in trying to overcome the issue and to avoid the war. That was what was being discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It was something that was very close to people's hearts and their interests, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Because it affected their lives, where they lived, their prosperity and their right to a peaceful existence, correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Those issues were much more complicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm just reducing them to their simplest here to save sometime. That encapsulates I suggest the sorts of issues that people were concerned about or the concerns people had. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Whether you're not sure or not, those things were all very personal, emotional things to the members of the three communities, correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Well, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When people discussed, members of the communities discussed the issues, these sorts of issues, relating to cantonisation or the division of Bosnia or remaining within Yugoslavia, people had fairly firm and strong views on these things, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes. It involved the right to self-determination, which should be equally applicable on all peoples. We Serbs believed that if the other people, peoples, were entitled to secession that equally we had the right to remain within a federal state.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When the communities or their representatives discussed these issues at meetings, they did so forcefully in presenting their views with some vigour, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with vigour but I would say that they were certainly very interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It would be fair to say that the representatives of each of the communities had their -- three communities, had their own views as to what should happen in Bosnia-Herzegovina, in April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, while it's not strictly form of objection but I think it would be fair for this witness if the question was more specific or more specific, when, where, among which ethnic groups, because otherwise it might be on the level of Bosnia on the level of region on the level of municipality. Otherwise it's not so clear this line of questions, what the position of -- and the line of questioning of Prosecution is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, my last question, Your Honour, was representatives had their own views as to what should happen in Bosnia in April, 1992, I'm obviously and I've said this before talking about the three constituent nations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes for the whole Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's right. It's a general question. I'm going to make it more specific.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What I'm suggesting to you is the views of the people or the representatives of the three communities were expressing were views they held quite strongly and expressed quite strongly in discussions with other representatives of other ethnic communities?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I can only speak of what I directly participated in. However, in these negotiations in which I took part, all of these things were much at a more normal level. I would even say quite polite. We, the Serbs, were not deprived of our rights by the Croats or by the Muslims to have our own views. Instead, there was an attempt to find a solution just to avoid a war, and we did discuss some kind of division within that framework we arrived at this plan on cantonisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A meeting -- you gave evidence earlier about a meeting in the town of Bosanski Samac in April, 1992 at which the representatives of the political parties and others attended to discuss these issues, correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The meeting was attended by representatives of the SDA, correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sulejman Tihic was there as a representative of the SDA, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I think that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: As was Izet Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. Probably he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic sitting over there was there as a representative of the SDP?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At this moment I have to intervene. There was no such information nor by any witness. Mr. Pisarevic definitely wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My reading of the transcripts was that Mr. Tihic said that he was there as a representative of the SDP. I can check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can check.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If Your Honour will just give me a moment. The transcript at page 1303 seems to indicate that Mr. Pisarevic was there but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you just read it out, which witness? Who is the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic in examination by Mr. Di Fazio on the 14th of September, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, there were a couple of meetings so I believe there might be some confusion. There was another meeting held in the municipality of -- actually it was, I don't know whether it was in Spomen Dom or some other place where Mr. Pisarevic was present but definitely not this. In local community now, Mr. Pisarevic is jogging my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's not particularly important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's what I was about to ask. Why don't you move on?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If I'm in error I withdraw any suggestion that Mr. Pisarevic was there and I stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mato Nusoic [phoen] was there as a representative of the HDZ, that's the Croat community, correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I don't remember the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The name of the gentleman is Mato Nuic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I stand corrected I was taking it from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Colonel Djurdjevic of the JNA was there, correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And Colonel Nikolic was also there, possibly representing the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: At this meeting that I was referring to, he wasn't present.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The meeting you were referring to, is that one that Dr. Simic chaired himself?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And was that the meeting at which he said, at the end, after the discussion of the possible division into -- the division of the area into Croat, Serb, and Muslim municipalities, you gave evidence of that before, is this the meeting at the end of which Dr. Simic said you have by Wednesday time to state your views whether in favour of this division or not. If you do not accept these proposals the Serbs will know what to undertake? Was that the meeting you attended?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I don't remember these words uttered by Dr. Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you say you don't remember, you have no positive memory of him either saying it or not saying it? Is that the situation?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: He didn't say that at the official meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If he said it would have been at a different meeting at which you weren't present; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, calling for speculation. How this witness the suggestion to know on which meeting if any meeting was and what was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's a fair objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In did -- the period late -- sorry, late 1990 through to mid-1992, you were I think you said the -- was it the local municipal SDS president?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you -- I think was your evidence that you weren't working full time in a job but were did I voting a lot of your time to SDS political activities?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: You have encompassed a rather long period of time. Including the time when I worked in the Napredak company and the working hours lasted until 3.00 p.m. and of course over the weekends I also had time for my party work. After the mobilisation, after I had been mobilised to military units, which took place in December, 1991, I also was most often free after 3.00 p.m. and over weekends, because that was sort of a peace time military drill, exercise, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The period you're speaking of was a period of intense political activity in Bosnia-Herzegovina, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you were the -- were you the local may [Realtime transcript read in error "mayor"] -- were you the main contact person for the SDS in the Bosanski Samac or Gradacac area?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just intervention I do apologise to my learned friend, it's page 77 line 1, it's a little bit not so clear in this transcript, the words "were you the local mayor"? I do believe that I didn't heard that in question of my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Quite correct. I didn't say "mayor." I'll ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you the main political contact person for the SDS in the Gradacac area in that period?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Contacts with whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you the -- were you the main SDS person in Gradacac at that area -- in that period, as the president of the municipal board, branch of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want to ask you about the structure of the SDS. The SDS was organised into local -- on a local and a national level, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And it had local branches with members attending meetings and voting on motions and so on as with a normal political party?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, basically.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And is it true that you convened meetings at the SDS membership and coordinated SDS party activities in the Gradacac area?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes. At the local level, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And as the local president, you were of course were in contact with the national party, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Well, the party functioned in a slightly different manner. In addition to a local level, and the leadership at the level of the republic, there existed also the main board at the level of the republic, and this board was a sort of link between the local leadership and the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And who were the members of the -- of that board, the republic level board in that period, the end of 1990 to mid-1992?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: At the republic level, Dr. Radovan Karadzic, Momcilo Krajisnik, Biljana, Velibor Ostojic, and many others, I don't know exactly who.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Biljana, was that Biljana Plavsic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, Biljana Plavsic. I forgot to mention Dr. Nikola Koljevic. He was also in the leadership of the party.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And it's correct to say that the two preeminent and controlling figures in the SDS leadership at that time were Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I remember that Dr. Biljana Plavsic was vice-president. So person number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So you'd -- to Karadzic and Krajisnik you'd add Plavsic as the preeminent and controlling figures in the SDS at that time, would you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: It's common knowledge. Dr. Karadzic was president and Mrs. Plavsic was vice-president. I have nothing to add to that. That was how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The SDS leadership, that is Karadzic, Krajisnik, and Plavsic, issued orders and directives from above to the local SDS branches and memberships such as yours, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Well, you say issued directives. It seems to me as if that had been a kind of military organisation. However, it was a political party within which we had two-way and democratic communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The leadership at the top level, that's Karadzic, Krajisnik, and Plavsic were responsible for the setting of policy, the decisions -- decisions on deciding upon policy, within the SDS, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I cannot agree with you. All the main political guidelines were adopted by the main board of the Serb Democratic Party. And Dr. Karadzic, as president, carried out these political decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And one of the -- I'm sorry, the -- I withdraw that. The leadership was also responsible for setting the strategic objectives of the SDS and the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Your questions somehow are very general, not to say imprecise.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm talking about the general structure of the SDS in Bosnia at the time, that is late 1990 to mid-1992, and I'm suggesting to you that the leadership was responsible for making decisions on strategic objectives of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: As the local president of the SDS -- I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. THE ACCUSED SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours I beg your pardon, my lawyer does not wish to react and this was not part of the examination-in-chief. This witness cannot speak about this, nor does he know about this. And I have very poor cooperation with my lawyer and I don't know what to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If you have any problems, those are matters for the Registrar, but the intervention in court during the proceedings will be done by your counsel. And there is nothing objectionable to the questions being put by Mr. Re to the witness. So Mr. Re can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I was going to ask you as the local president of the SDS, you've already agreed you were the contact point for communication with the board of the party, you were also responsible, were you not, for implementing party decisions within the area which you were the president, I'm sorry, party policy in the area of which you were president, correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And at this time, when the Republika Srpska was being established and new governmental organisations were being put in place, an army was being formed, that's the VRS, it was very important for the local SDS to have good lines of communication with the SDS leadership through the board, correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: At which time exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Still talking about the same time frame, which is when the Republika Srpska was being formed, that's the end of -- I'm sorry, make that the end of 1990 -- say, October 1991 through to mid-1992.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, Republika Srpska was established on the 9th of January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My question to you was: At that period, when the Republika Srpska was being established, new government organisations were being formed, municipalities were being formed, the VRS was establishing itself as an army with a separate name, it was important for the local SDS to have good lines of communication with the national leadership, national board, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: First of all, the army was not established until May, 1992. Before the army was established, the work of all political organisations was banned in Republika Srpska, also in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The leaders, Krajisnik, Plavsic, and Karadzic remained members of the SDS at that time when you say political activity was banned, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You remained a member of the SDS at the time when you say political activity was banned, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remained a member, but the party was not operating.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: As far as you know, none of Krajisnik, Plavsic, or Karadzic resigned their membership of the SDS in that period, did they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the lines of communication remained open between the local SDS, that's the one where you were, and the national SDS, correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: You mean while the conflict was breaking out?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: No. There was no communication between the leadership and politics, because communication, as far as I know, took place between the leadership of Republika Srpska and the official authorities at local level. The party was not the authorities. For example, we in Pelagicevo establish the municipality of Pelagicevo for that reason, and it was in charge of communicating with the state leadership. The official representatives of government.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And as far as you know, the official representatives of government of both levels in that period communicated, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The local level of government, the municipal assemblies, put into place decisions or implemented decisions of the national assembly, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: You know, you are now putting a question to me in relation to something that I did not participate in. At that time, after the conflict broke out, I was a soldier, and I did not meddle in the functioning of civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Crisis Staffs or War Presidencies were established on local levels as a result of SDS party directives, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I am not informed about that. Because this was probably done after the conflict had broken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So are you saying you're unable to answer any questions about the political structure or situation after the conflict broke out?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes, because after the conflict broke out, I did not take part in any of these contacts or in the work of the civilian authorities. I don't know about that. Any answer I might give would be sheer guess work.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The conflict broke out in April, 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You of course were elected vice-president of the municipal assembly in either February or March, 1992?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I was elected vice-president on the 29th of February, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you remained in that position until when?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: In fact, I never exercised the powers of that office, because all of this was merely declarative. That office did not carry any weight, absolutely, because I did not even have a proper office. I did not receive a salary. Absolutely. I don't know how to express myself actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's not what I asked you. I asked you when you remained in that position until, from the 29th of February 1992 until when were you the vice-president of the municipal assembly, of the Serb assembly?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: I repeat I was elected on the 29th of February and I remained in that position until the war conflict broke out, and this position, this office, just withered away on its own.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So you're saying the position didn't exist; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: In fact, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I take it the same with the president of the Serb assembly, that position didn't exist either?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: On paper, that position did exist, but that was not exercised either.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what about the executive council? Is that another paper fiction? The executive council of the municipality of -- the Bosnia -- sorry, the Serb municipality? Another paper fiction?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes. The one who was elected was only there on paper, and never functioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The president of the executive council, again another fiction was it, paper fiction?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff, another fiction?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: There was no Crisis Staff even on paper, because it was never elected or established.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: War Presidency didn't exist either?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: If you mean the working Presidency, the chair of the meeting, that is a different thing. That did exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just a correction. There has been a misunderstanding. The Prosecutor asked him about the War Presidency and the witness received interpretation saying working Presidency. And this confuses the witness, which is obvious from his last answer. So could the Prosecutor please clarify this with the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I think the question can be repeated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, also in addition maybe my learned friend can be more precise, if he is speaking about Crisis Staff, to be more precise and more specific.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: To which period he's referring because otherwise it's too large, it may be in January of 1992 or December, 1991 or July, 1992, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: With respect to my learned friend the answer was quite specific there was no Crisis Staff even on paper because it was never elected or established. That covers every eventuality which Mr. Pantelic has just raised. Never. You can't be more specific than that in an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The answer of the witness is as you say, Mr. Re. But the other matter pointed out by Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Look, the War Presidency in Bosanski Samac, or Pelagicevo was that another fiction, something that didn't exist? Not elected, not appointed? Just on paper?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: My role ended on the 28th of March, 1992, at that last session. Everything that happened afterwards, or that happened in the territory of the municipality of Samac, I don't know about that. I did not participate in it and it is only natural that I can't give answers about this. Whatever I would say would amount to hearsay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So you can't give the Tribunal, sorry, the Trial Chamber, any evidence about anything that happened in Bosanski Samac politically from the 28th of March, 1992, is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Re, I find this a little confusing, simply because in the witness summary, we have been directed that this witness will testify to the following facts, including the creation of Crisis Staff and its activities, and the defendant Dr. Simic's activities in capacity of president of the Crisis Staff. So I'm finding I must say this all a little perplexing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Presumably, Your Honour, the witness didn't prepare the summary so I can't really ask him what's in the summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You didn't take any notes -- I withdraw that. When -- the meeting you attended of the Serb assembly, the first one, that's the 29th of February, 1992, minutes were taken of that meeting, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Well, probably so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And as far as you know, as the vice-president or perhaps the non-existent vice-president of a non-existent assembly, decisions were numbered when they were taken, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You didn't take notes yourself at any meetings you attended, did you, decisions?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't take any.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So you're relying entirely upon your own memory 11 years after the event when you say as far as you can recall, decisions weren't numbered; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And if decisions -- numbered decisions appeared in the Official Gazette of the Samac municipality, published nine years ago, you'd agree that they would be more accurate than your memory now, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: No. They could not be more accurate because I know full well what had not been adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: But of course, having no participation in politics, the assembly or anything after the 28th of March, 1992, you can't give the Trial Chamber any accurate evidence as to the accuracy of the gazette, for anything that happened after that date, can you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: As for this Official Gazette, I can only testify about matters that pertained to the 29th of February and the 28th of March. As for later, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: But in doing so you're relying entirely upon your memory because you had no notes of what happened at those meetings, correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC
utterances.text: There is no need for me to -- well, to explain this to you, I know that no Crisis Staffs were established because there was no need for that, and at that time, none of us were that smart that we could assume that a war would break out until the very last day, we hoped that that would not happen. So I know for sure that no Crisis Staffs were established.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I start with my re-examination, due to the fact that my client just raised, it's a very serious matter, I'm fully surprised with this so I kindly ask for the adjournment and I have to consult with my client because with this approach, I don't know in which direction I have to -- maybe I can get additional instructions or to clarify this with my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You remember I did say these are matters for the Registrar to deal with if there is any change of mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but my duty, Your Honour, is even for short period of time to see what's going on, maybe it's a matter of kind of anxiety or some other personal problems or something deeper, because that's for the first time at this hearing today I heard this approach. It's fully surprising matter for me, Your Honour. So I really am in an embarrassing situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution would not object to my learned friend having an adjournment for purposes of a conference with his client to clarify any matters before re-examination. It's in fairness for a fair trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And if I may add, Your Honour, if it's appropriate for this Trial Chamber, maybe we could adjourn, I cannot be limited for minutes or period. I don't know how much time I would need to confer. Maybe it's wise to adjourn for today because it's really serious matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pantelic, you just discuss with your client. The Trial Chamber will give you ten minutes to deal with that because there is no reason at all that the Trial Chamber has to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I am also aware about the basis so I will try to find out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We will rise for ten minutes, we shall continue at 1535. --- Break taken at 3.25 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, please, re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, after the short meeting with my client, he informed me that he doesn't have a confidence in my work that I am not acting in his interest. He mentioned something that he doesn't know for which service or which department within this Tribunal and outside I am working. It was very heavy discussion. He's very upset and he's very nervous, a lot of -- I would say, heavy issues and things he raised and put on my account. So I really don't think that I should proceed today with the remaining of the re-examination. Maybe in the interests of my client and following the standards here within the Tribunal, maybe we could have an additional time for conferring or maybe my client can raise that issue with the Registrar and try to find out what shall we do at this particular stage of proceedings, or maybe if you need some more details, maybe he can address the Trial Chamber or he can proceed on the other way, because otherwise, I really don't see any possibility, speaking for today, to finish and to act in accordance with my duties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Where is Mr. Vukovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He's apparently not in The Hague due to the problems with the -- with visa proceedings. The registry is taking care about that, I believe, sometimes in the beginning of next week, he should be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We will adjourn until tomorrow. In the meantime, the Trial Chamber is requesting the Office of the Registrar to deal with the matter and give the Trial Chamber a report before the end of the sitting hours today. The Trial Chamber would like to tell the accused person that the Registrar has got the rules by which these matters are handled, and unless the Registrar is satisfied that there is a good reason to change counsel or to appoint somebody else to replace Mr. Pantelic, that would depend on what the accused -- what reasons the accused gives the Office of the Registrar so this is a very serious matter and it has to be dealt with promptly. We will adjourn and continue our proceedings tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: 3.42 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 10th day of January, 2003, at 9:30 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
